final_post_text:
If you store OLTP data in the same schema as your analytics, you’re courting a performance disaster. 🏗️  

Every transaction hits the same row store that your BI queries scan, leading to lock contention, p99 latency spikes, and disk I/O thrashing. 🔄  

The core of the issue is that OLTP systems are built for low‑latency, ACID, row‑oriented workloads. In contrast, OLAP thrives on columnar, denormalised storage that compresses and parallelises scans.  

When you force the same schema onto both, you pay in both directions: transactional throughput drops because analytical scans lock rows; analytical queries stall because they have to read uncompressed row pages.  

A proven pattern is a one‑way stream: OLTP -> CDC -> OLAP. Capture changes with a change‑data‑capture engine, then transform and load into a columnar store. This keeps each layer optimized for its workload.  

• Row‑store, 3NF, ACID, low latency  
• Column‑store, denormalised, high compression, high throughput 📊  

Rule of thumb: Keep OLTP row‑store and OLAP columnar store separate; stream and transform changes before analytics.  

What CDC solutions and transformation pipelines have you deployed to keep OLTP and OLAP separate in your production stack?

source_evidence:
OLTP (Online Transaction Processing):
- Is used for live transactional system where we need to access data in high concurrency low latency mode.
- To achieve this Milliseconds latency and high concurrency operations. It is preferred to have data is highly normalised (3rd normal form)
- Data remained stored in row-oriented format 8-16 KB to get entire results in one read
- Fast read, write and update concurrency, and transactional integrity are required. Vertical scaling
- Priority remains low latency and write integrity. Build around strict ACID compliance

OLAP (Online Analytical Processing)
- It is used for complex analytical aggregations with historical data.
- Read heavy: read huge amount of data with higher latency. It is expected to have denormalized(Star Schema/ Snowflake Schema/ Wide Tables)
- Data remained in columnar format (Parquet or Delta), This columnar storage help high compression, High I/O savings, columnar layouts usually improve large scans, compression, and aggregations.
- Scanning huge amount of data latency remain seconds to minutes. Scale horizontally.
- Priority remains high throughput read performance

In modern data word these 2 system communicate with each other using CDC Change Data Capture(CDC) and ETL/ELT

technical_analysis.core_lesson: OLTP prioritizes low‑latency, ACID compliance with row‑oriented, highly normalised data, while OLAP prioritises high‑throughput analytical queries on columnar, denormalised storage
technical_analysis.common_misconception: Assuming OLTP and OLAP can share the same schema and storage format without performance penalties
technical_analysis.practical_takeaway: Use CDC to stream changes from OLTP to OLAP, but design separate schemas: keep OLTP row‑store for transactional integrity, and transform data into columnar, denormalised form for analytics
technical_analysis.useful_comparison: Row‑store & 3NF & ACID & low latency vs Column‑store & denormalised & high compression & high throughput
